EXPLANATION: The intense high-frequency band at 3545 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a free O–H stretching vibration, implying the molecule must contain an –OH group; only candidate 7 (O=BC(=O)O), which possesses a carboxylic-acid-type –COOH moiety, fits this requirement. Its –OH stretch can appear near 3550 cm⁻¹ when the hydrogen is not strongly H-bonded. The strong 1053 cm⁻¹ line is consistent with a C–O stretch of the –COOH group, while the weaker 1370 cm⁻¹ band matches the in-plane δ(OH) or ν_s(OCO) deformation/bending mode often observed for carboxylic acids in the 1350-1400 cm⁻¹ region. No other candidate contains an O–H (or N–H) bond to account for the 3545 cm⁻¹ band, making 7 the most compatible choice despite the limited data.
